svg.aria-label: AD5328 module V1.2, reconstructed from photos: a 6-pin logic header and a 100 ohm array feed an AD5328 DAC; each of its 8 outputs drives one half of an SGM8272 op-amp wired as a difference amplifier with a gain of 4 against the 2.5 V reference, giving plus or minus 10 V on terminals AO1 to AO8; a TPS61040 boost converter, a charge pump and 78L12/79L12 regulators make plus and minus 12 V for the op-amps.
svg.text: AD5328 module V1.2 (AD5328模块 V1.2) · schematic reconstructed from photos
Solid: read from the board (silkscreen, part codes, IC markings) or from the parts' data sheets, or the only way those parts can work together.
Dashed: inferred from where the parts sit; the traces are not visible. Check with a meter before relying on it.
seen or from a data sheet
Same 5 V as H1 pin 6: feed one of the two.
Each output drives one stage (right): A → AO1 … H → AO8.
The order is presumed, not traced.
Jumper on 1-2 (as drawn): the onboard 2.5 V is VREF, the normal
setting. Jumper off: an external reference goes into pin 2 (EX),
and the output range scales with it (±4 · VREF at DAC gain ×2).
Never bridge 2-3: it shorts VREF to ground (with 1-2 also fitted,
U9's output too). U9's part number is not visible; R49 100 Ω (01A),
R50 0 Ω and C36-C38 sit beside it, their wiring is not visible.
Eight copies, two per dual op-amp (U4, U5, U7, U8). Resistor codes as printed on every stage.
Both pairs are 1 : 4 (3 k : 12 k and 30 k : 120 k): a difference amplifier with a gain of 4.
If the DAC drives the 3 kΩ side instead, the sign flips: AOx = 10 V − 4 · VOUTx (see the meter check below).
WHAT IS READ, WHAT IS INFERRED
connectors, silkscreen, test pads, IC markings and every resistor code: 302 = 3 kΩ,
01A = 100 Ω, 01D = 100 kΩ, 30B = 2 kΩ. U2's marking PHOI = TI TPS61040 (SOT-23-5).
from the data sheets: AD5328 (ADI Rev. F), SGM8272 (SGMICRO), TPS61040 (TI SLVS413L).
the part numbers of U9, Q1 and D2, all capacitor values, the traces under the parts.
power off, continuity from U6 pin 4 (VOUTA) to AO1's resistors: a 30 kΩ (303) means
the drawing is right, a 3 kΩ (302) that the sign is flipped. The power-on reading agrees:
about −10 V on every AO as drawn, +10 V if flipped (CALIBRATION.md §1, step 3).
SUPPLY · 5 V IN, ±12 V FOR THE OP-AMPS
L1, R6 (0 Ω), C14 and C15 sit by the 5V pad and U4: probably a filter on the
5 V of the DAC or the op-amps. Not traced. The AD5328 takes 2.5 V to 5.5 V,
so the module's 5 V must stay at or below 5.5 V.
